hook: A mission report (MISREP) filed by the 482nd Attack Squadron documenting a 19-hour ISR sortie over Iraq on December 1–2, 2022, during which the crew observed a single possible UAP/UAV flying west to east near Baghdad at FL180, captured on FMV and submitted to AARO.
why_it_matters: This document is notable as a firsthand operational military report generated during an active combat ISR mission under Operation INHERENT RESOLVE, not a retrospective or investigative file. The UAP was logged with a precise grid reference near Baghdad and a specific contact time (1620Z), yet the crew recorded no detectable signatures and chose not to pursue it, illustrating standard operational protocol when UAP are encountered mid-mission. The accompanying ten-second infrared video — showing an area of contrast transiting the sensor field-of-view — provides rare visual documentation of a UAP contact in a combat zone.
key_findings: At 1620Z on December 1, 2022, the crew observed one possible UAP/UAV flying west to east in the vicinity of grid 38SMB4[redacted]83[redacted] near Baghdad, Iraq, while operating at FL180 (18,000 feet).
The crew did not follow the UAP and continued the mission as tasked; no further UAP events were observed for the remainder of the sortie.
No UAP signatures were detected, no RF frequency or duration was recorded, and effects on persons were explicitly reported as 'NONE REPORTED.'
The mission was a 19-hour 17-minute ISR/TARGET DEV sortie with primary sensor FMV; the aircraft also collected SIGINT via AIRHANDLER, and FMV footage was exploited by DGS-AR.
The report was filed by the 482ATKS under USCENTCOM/Operation INHERENT RESOLVE and declassified by MG Richard A. Harrison, USCENTCOM Chief of Staff, on 8 October 2025 for release to AARO.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: The MISREP was explicitly submitted to and declassified for release to AARO, making it a direct input into AARO's UAP reporting and resolution pipeline.

The document is part of the PURSUE public disclosure release, which reflects congressionally mandated UAP transparency efforts, and its declassification references multiple MDR numbers consistent with structured legislative-driven review.
